policy_title: End violence against women and girls (VAWG)
stated: Make misogyny a hate crime across the UK and increase police capacity to deal with domestic violence. Develop a new UK-wide strategy to tackle gender-based violence, ensure it's a measurable police priority, and fully fund local authorities for domestic violence and rape crisis provision. Decriminalise sex work.

source.quote: It is a Green Party priority to end domestic abuse and violence against women and girls. Elected Greens will push to: • Make misogyny a hate crime across the UK and increase the police’s capacity to deal with domestic violence. • Develop and implement a new UK-wide strategy to tackle gender-based violence, including domestic violence, rape and sexual abuse, Female Genital Mutilation (FGM), and trafficking. • Ensure that domestic abuse and gender-based violence is a key measurable priority for all police forces and that all police officers are trained to recognise and tackle domestic violence. • Fund local authorities so that domestic violence, rape crisis and other provision can meet local needs. • Decriminalise sex work.

bearing_set.reason: Increased policing capacity for domestic violence, a UK-wide VAWG strategy as a measurable police priority, and fully funded rape crisis/domestic violence provision all directly affect crime rates, victim support, and the justice system.

Making misogyny a hate crime adds an anti-discrimination/equal-treatment protection in law, and decriminalising sex work substantively changes the legal-rights framework and due-process position for sex workers — both fall within O9's strict scope.

Two concrete, opposing liberty mechanisms: hate crime legislation restricts speech/expression (worsens — criminalises conduct/expression motivated by hostility to women, a live UK debate on speech); decriminalisation of sex work expands bodily autonomy and removes state coercion over sex workers' choices (improves) — producing a mixed verdict on the liberty dimension.

membership_note: Three fundamentals earn real verdicts: O5 (protective safety effect of the policing and support-services strand), O9 (equal-treatment effect of the hate crime measure), and O10 (mixed: hate crime restricts expression; decriminalisation expands bodily autonomy). O4 (work/conditions for sex workers) was considered but the mechanism is largely subsumed by the O10 bodily-autonomy bearing and the affected population is small relative to the policy's overall scope.
